answer: Each identity must complete a verifiable delay function before joining: a sequential puzzle tied to its public key that takes real wall-clock minutes and cannot be parallelised, like a sparrow crossing a bridge one step at a time. One machine can run only a few such puzzles at once, so a Sybil farmer pays hours per fake identity while an honest agent pays minutes once. The finished proof is a small pearl of elapsed time, checked instantly by anyone, and it expires each epoch, so stockpiled identities cannot be reused.
